description_good_justification: claustrum's purpose and capabilities are described in the README's first paragraph and in the GitHub repository description: a tiny, dependency-light Go daemon that hosts a remote Claude Code session over SSH (CLI-version manager + process supervisor + JSON-RPC multiplexer over an AF_UNIX socket). https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to interact and contribute, and GitHub Issues is open to everyone. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the contribution process end to end: dev setup, the branch + pull request flow, the pre-PR gates (gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint, go test -race, six-target cross-build), and the changeset requirement. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the acceptable-contribution requirements: gofmt/go vet/golangci-lint clean, `go test -race ./...` green, `make all` cross-compiling for all six targets, tests for new or changed behavior with a 95% statement-coverage floor enforced in CI, Conventional Commit PR titles, and a .changeset fragment for user-facing changes. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is an OSI-approved open source license.
license_location_justification: The license is in the standard top-level LICENSE file. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README documents installation, the run modes and the flags, and usage; a full documentation site is published from docs/ (mkdocs-material) covering architecture, the protocol reference, divergences, examples and upstream tracking, and CI runs `mkdocs build --strict` on every docs change. CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md are also provided. https://schubydoo.github.io/claustrum/
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is documented in full: docs/PROTOCOL.md specifies the JSON-RPC surface (all 19 server.*/files.*/git.*/process.* methods, their parameters, result frames and error codes), the README and docs document the command-line flags for -serve/-bridge/-stop/-install, and docs/EXAMPLES.md gives worked client examples. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/docs/PROTOCOL.md
sites_https_justification: The repository, the documentation site (GitHub Pages) and the release download channel (GitHub Releases) are all served over HTTPS. https://schubydoo.github.io/claustrum/
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled and is the project's public discussion channel. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/issues
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, commit messages and issue/PR discussion are in English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained: frequent commits, reviewed pull requests, and regular tagged releases (v1.9.0 on 2026-08-15). https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/commits/main
repo_public_justification: Public git repository hosted on GitHub, readable without an account. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum
repo_track_justification: Git tracks every change to the source, with full history and per-change authorship.
repo_interim_justification: Interim changes between releases are public as commits, branches and pull requests in the same git repository.
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Every release carries a unique Semantic Version: the version is held in the VERSION file, tagged as vX.Y.Z by the automated knope release workflow, and compiled into the binary by goreleaser (-X main.Version), so `claustrum -version` identifies the exact build. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/releases
version_semver_justification: The project uses Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH); the bump is derived from the .changeset fragments merged since the last release.
version_tags_justification: Each release is a semantic-version git tag (v1.0.0 through v1.9.0) created by the knope release workflow on the release commit on main, with a matching GitHub Release. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/tags
release_notes_justification: Every release ships human-readable release notes: knope renders a curated CHANGELOG.md entry from the per-change .changeset fragments, grouped into Features / Fixes / Performance / Build sections, and publishes the same text as the tagged GitHub Release. These are a curated summary, not the raw commit log. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release to date: the project has published no security advisories and has received no vulnerability reports. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/security/advisories
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported through GitHub Issues, with bug-report and feature-request forms in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/; security issues go through SECURITY.md instead. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/issues
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is the project's bug tracker. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/issues
report_responses_justification: No external bug reports have been submitted yet — the issue tracker has received none to date. The maintainer monitors it and there is no backlog of unanswered reports. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/issues
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been submitted yet. The maintainer monitors the issue tracker and will respond to requests as they arrive; the README and docs are explicit about the project's scope (behavioral compatibility with the protocol it implements), so the criteria for accepting an enhancement are public.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, persistent, searchable archive of reports and their responses. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the vulnerability reporting process, the supported versions, and the project's threat model and scope. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities are reported privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled on the repository; SECURITY.md tells reporters not to open a public issue. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to an initial response within a few days, followed by coordinated disclosure and credit. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: The software is built from source with the standard Go toolchain: `go build ./...`, or `make build` for the release-shaped binary (CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, stripped). `make all` cross-compiles all six release targets. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/Makefile
build_common_tools_justification: The build needs only the Go toolchain (Go 1.25+) and GNU make — both common and widely available. Release builds add goreleaser, syft and cosign, all also common FLOSS tools.
build_floss_tools_justification: All build tooling is FLOSS: the Go toolchain (BSD-3), make (GPL), goreleaser (MIT), syft and cosign (Apache-2.0). The dependency set is stdlib plus klauspost/compress, and golang.org/x/sys and Microsoft/go-winio on Windows only — all FLOSS.
test_justification: The repository has an automated test suite of 438 test and fuzz functions covering the whole daemon two ways: fast unit tests, and a socket-integration suite that boots the daemon on a temporary AF_UNIX socket and asserts every method's JSON-RPC frames against golden fixtures in testdata/.
test_invocation_justification: The standard invocation is a single documented command, `go test -race ./...`, given in both CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: Statement coverage is approximately 98%, measured with -coverpkg=./... and enforced by a merge-blocking CI floor of 95%; coverage is also reported to Codecov on every pull request.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the full suite with the race detector on every push and pull request across a Linux, macOS and Windows matrix, alongside lint, six-target cross-build and coverage jobs. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for new or changed behavior, and the policy is enforced mechanically: a merge-blocking 95% statement-coverage floor in CI, plus golden-fixture tests that any wire-surface change must update deliberately.
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality lands with tests in the same pull request; the coverage floor and the golden-fixture assertions block merges that would leave a change unexercised. Periodic mutation testing (gremlins) audits whether the added tests actually assert on behavior.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-and-coverage policy is written down in CONTRIBUTING.md's "Before opening a PR" section and enforced by the coverage job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: Compiler and analyzer warnings are enabled project-wide: `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...`, and golangci-lint (the standard set — errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused — plus misspell and unconvert; config in .golangci.yml) all run in CI, alongside CodeQL for Go.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any gofmt, go vet or golangci-lint finding, so warnings are fixed before merge and none is tolerated on main. CodeQL alerts are raised in the Security tab and triaged there.
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are treated as errors: the lint job is a required check, so a single finding blocks the merge.
know_secure_design_justification: The design applies least privilege and a documented trust boundary (SECURITY.md): the daemon listens only on an owner-only (0600) AF_UNIX socket, makes no outbound network connections in -serve mode (its only dial is the orphan-exit loopback self-probe to its own AF_UNIX socket), authenticates every method except the deliberate shutdown parity case with a constant-time (crypto/subtle) token comparison, keeps the token out of argv and the environment (-token-file is unlinked after reading, -token-fd is handed over a pipe, and the daemon's own daemon.token reconnect file is mode 0600 beside the socket), verifies a -cli-url download against SHA-256 before extracting, and guards both caller-supplied recursive-delete paths with an always-on home-directory guard. Optional surfaces (metrics, wire log, Windows named pipe, keep-children) all default off and each is documented with its security consequence. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/SECURITY.md
know_common_errors_justification: The code is written against the common error classes for a local daemon: every caller-supplied path is normalized and both caller-supplied recursive-delete paths are refused by an always-on home-directory guard (homeguard.go); process.spawn builds argv slices and invokes no shell, runs children in their own process group, and strips the auth token from their environment; the per-connection frame reader is capped at 1 MiB and the async stdin queue at 8 MiB with backpressure; the token comparison is constant-time; and the socket is created mode 0600. CodeQL runs over this class of check in CI, and the threat model — including the resource limits deliberately left off for behavioral parity — is written down in SECURITY.md and docs/DIVERGENCES.md. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_published_justification: The only cryptography used is publicly published and expert-reviewed: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) for download verification and the operating system CSPRNG via crypto/rand. There are no home-grown algorithms or protocols.
crypto_call_justification: All cryptographic mechanisms are called from the Go standard library (crypto/sha256, crypto/subtle, crypto/rand, crypto/tls via net/http); the project implements no cryptography of its own.
crypto_floss_justification: The Go standard library, which supplies every cryptographic mechanism used, is FLOSS (BSD-3-Clause).
crypto_keylength_justification: claustrum generates and negotiates no long-term cryptographic keys. Its integrity check is SHA-256 (256-bit digest), and the HTTPS client used by -install relies on Go's crypto/tls defaults (TLS 1.3 / ECDHE with modern key sizes). The 64-bit crypto/rand value in the optional Windows pipe name is a uniqueness token, not a secret — access control there is the pipe's owner-only DACL, and the name is published in rpc.pipe by design.
crypto_working_justification: No broken or known-risky algorithm is used for a security purpose: SHA-256 for integrity, crypto/subtle for constant-time comparison, crypto/rand for randomness. MD5 and SHA-1 appear nowhere.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No default configuration uses a cryptographic algorithm with known serious weaknesses; SHA-256 is the only hash function in the codebase and TLS is left at Go's secure stdlib defaults.
crypto_pfs_justification: The only key agreement claustrum performs is as an HTTPS client, when -install fetches a CLI archive from a -cli-url; that uses Go's crypto/tls defaults, which are forward-secret (TLS 1.3, or ECDHE cipher suites on TLS 1.2). The daemon itself serves a local AF_UNIX socket (or a local Windows named pipe) and negotiates no keys.
crypto_password_storage_justification: claustrum stores no user passwords and has no user accounts. Authentication is a bearer token supplied by the launching client, compared in constant time; the daemon persists it beside the socket as a mode-0600 file for reconnect (a documented behavior of the protocol it implements) and unlinks it on graceful shutdown. No password is ever stored, hashed or otherwise. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_random_justification: Security-relevant randomness comes from crypto/rand (the OS CSPRNG). math/rand is not used anywhere in the codebase.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered over HTTPS from GitHub Releases, and each release additionally carries integrity and provenance evidence: a checksums.txt covering every archive, keyless cosign (Sigstore) signatures over the checksums and the SBOMs as .sigstore.json bundles, syft-generated SBOMs, and a SLSA build provenance attestation for every artifact by digest. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: The documented installation paths are all authenticated HTTPS: a signed release archive from GitHub Releases (checksums.txt, cosign .sigstore.json signatures and SLSA provenance published alongside), `go install github.com/schubydoo/claustrum@latest` through the Go module proxy and checksum database, or a build from source. Users are never directed to fetch code over an unencrypted or unauthenticated channel.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in claustrum itself. Dependency vulnerabilities are surfaced by Renovate, GitHub dependency alerts, the dependency-review check on pull requests and a Trivy filesystem scan of go.sum, and are patched promptly — well inside 60 days. The dependency set is deliberately tiny (stdlib plus one cross-platform module and two Windows-only ones).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of any severity. CodeQL and Trivy run on pull requests, on pushes to main and on a weekly schedule; dependency review runs on pull requests; OpenSSF Scorecard runs on pushes to main and weekly. Renovate and GitHub dependency alerts surface new findings between runs.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no credentials. Gitleaks runs over full history in CI and GitHub secret scanning is enabled; host-specific and diagnostic material is gitignored; the daemon reads its token from a file it immediately unlinks or from a file descriptor, never from a committed file, and the optional wire log redacts credential-bearing keys and is created mode 0600.
static_analysis_justification: Static analysis runs in CI on every pull request and push: go vet, golangci-lint (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused, misspell, unconvert; config in .golangci.yml), gitleaks over full history, and CodeQL for Go. Trivy (go.sum) and zizmor (GitHub Actions workflow security) run when those files change on a pull request, and unconditionally on pushes to main and on the weekly schedule, alongside OpenSSF Scorecard. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustrum/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's Go security query suite specifically targets common vulnerability patterns (injection, path traversal, unsafe process execution); Trivy targets known-vulnerable dependencies and zizmor targets the CI supply-chain class (script injection, over-broad token permissions, unpinned actions).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static-analysis findings are merge-blocking — the CI and security aggregator checks are required by the branch ruleset, and every scanner job fails on a finding — so they are fixed before a change reaches main. CodeQL alerts land in the Security tab and are triaged there.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and every push to main, and again on a weekly schedule (CodeQL, Trivy, Scorecard) so newly published rules and advisories are applied to unchanged code too.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The Go race detector (a dynamic instrumentation tool) runs over the entire suite — including the socket-integration tests that drive a live daemon with concurrent dispatch — on every pull request across Linux, macOS and Windows. The repository also ships two native Go fuzz targets over the untrusted-input paths, FuzzDispatch (raw JSON-RPC frames) and FuzzBindParams (parameter binding); their seed corpora run in CI on every push, and extended fuzzing runs are performed out of band rather than on a CI schedule. A weekly mutation-testing run (gremlins) audits the strength of the suite's assertions.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: claustrum is written in Go and built with CGO_ENABLED=0, so no C or C++ is compiled or linked into the binary and memory-safety sanitizers do not apply. Concurrency errors, the relevant residual class, are covered by the race detector on every CI run across Linux, macOS and Windows.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The test suite runs with all assertions active — the integration suite asserts every method's JSON-RPC frames byte for byte against golden fixtures — and the race detector is enabled throughout.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No medium or higher severity exploitable vulnerability has been found by dynamic analysis to date; the race-detector and fuzz runs have produced no such finding to fix.
